title: Kth Missing Positive Number
hints: if the array had no gaps at all, arr[i] would always equal i+1 (1-indexed position). the actual gap between arr[i] and its 'expected' value i+1 tells you exactly how many positives are missing up through that point
define missing(i) = arr[i] - (i + 1). this count only increases or stays the same as i grows, since the array is strictly increasing - that monotonic property means you can binary search it
binary search for the smallest index i where missing(i) >= k. everything before that index has fewer than k missing numbers before it

once you find that boundary index i, the answer is k plus however many numbers from arr you've passed: specifically, answer = k + i, using the number of missing values already accounted for below arr[i-1] to place k precisely in the gap
commonMistakes: off-by-one errors in the missing(i) = arr[i] - (i+1) formula when using 0-indexed vs 1-indexed reasoning
using a linear scan when the array can be large enough that binary search is expected
forgetting the case where k is smaller than the first gap, i.e. the answer lies before arr[0]

content.problemStatement:
You're given a strictly increasing array of positive integers and an
integer `k`. Consider the sequence of all positive integers that are
NOT in the array.

**Return the `k`th number in that sequence.**
constraints: arr is strictly increasing and contains positive integers
notes: k is smaller than arr[0], so the answer is simply k
arr starts at 1 and has no gaps for a long stretch

missing positives in order are 5, 6, 7, ... the 2nd one is 6
missing positives in order are 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, ... the 3rd one is 3

optimal.pattern: index-based counting: at index i (0-indexed), the number of missing positives before arr[i] is arr[i] - (i + 1), since arr[i] would equal i+1 if nothing were missing; binary search this monotonic quantity for the first index where it reaches k

bruteForce.approach: walk through positive integers 1, 2, 3, ... one at a time, checking membership in arr (or advancing a pointer through arr), counting missing ones until you reach the kth
bruteForce.time: O(n + arr[-1]) in the worst case
